title: Graphing a Downward-Shifted Two-Thirds Power Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Analyze and describe the graph of y + 4 = x^(2/3) by solving for y and identifying its parent function, shift, cusp, domain, range, and intercepts.

steps.title: Solve Explicitly for y and Identify the Shift
steps.explanation: Subtracting 4 from both sides shows that the graph is the parent curve y = x^(2/3) shifted vertically downward by 4 units.
steps.why: Subtracting 4 from f(x) translates the graph down by 4 units.

steps.title: Determine the Cusp, Symmetry, Domain, and Range
steps.explanation: The even function y = x^(2/3) - 4 is symmetric about the y-axis, defined for all real x, and has its sharp cusp (global minimum) at the y-intercept (0, -4).
steps.why: Since x^(2/3) >= 0 with equality at x = 0, x^(2/3) - 4 >= -4.

steps.title: Find the x-Intercepts
steps.explanation: The two symmetric branches rise from (0, -4) through (-1, -3) and (1, -3) and cross the x-axis at (-8, 0) and (8, 0).
steps.why: Cubing both solutions of cbrt(x) = +/-2 yields x = +/-8.
